name: Fa'a'ā International Airport
before:
French Polynesia's international airport, on Tahiti just 5 km south west of Papeete.

It is built on the sea. There was not enough level ground on Tahiti, and rather than flatten large stretches of sloping farmland the airport was laid primarily on reclaimed land over the coral reef just offshore.

The single runway is 3,420 metres and takes aircraft up to a 747 or A380. Intercontinental flights reach France, the United States, Canada by way of the States, Chile, Japan and New Zealand.

For island hopping, Air Tahiti flies daily to most other islands in French Polynesia and has one international route, to the Cook Islands. Both Air Tahiti and Air Tahiti Nui have their head offices on the airport.

Buses run in from Papeete along the west coast freeway, which passes directly in front of the terminal.

The airport opened in 1960.
after:
French Polynesia's international airport, on Tahiti just 5 km south west of Papeete.

It is built on the sea, mostly on reclaimed land just offshore.

The single runway is 3,420 metres and takes aircraft up to a 747. Long-haul flights reach France, the United States, Japan and New Zealand.

For island hopping, Air Tahiti and Air Moana fly from here to the other islands, several times a day to the most popular ones. Air Tahiti also has one international route, to Rarotonga in the Cook Islands. The long-haul airline Air Tahiti Nui has its head office on the airport.

Taxis serve the terminal, and tour operators run transfers that can be booked ahead through a travel agent or the hotel.

claims.claim: long-haul flights reach France, the United States, Japan and New Zealand
claims.inAfter: Long-haul flights reach France, the United States, Japan and New Zealand.
claims.note: Was '... France, the United States, Canada by way of the States, Chile, Japan and New Zealand' (Canada and Chile cut below). SEAC's map of the 2025 scheduled international routes shows Paris CDG (Air Tahiti Nui, Air France, French Bee), Los Angeles, Seattle, San Francisco, Honolulu, Tokyo and Auckland, plus Nouméa, Nadi and Rarotonga. Air Tahiti Nui and Tahiti Tourisme name the same cities. 'Intercontinental' is kept from the old text, which took it from Wikipedia with New Zealand included. Review (24 Sep): 'Intercontinental' changed to 'Long-haul', because Tahiti and New Zealand are both in Oceania, so the Auckland flights are not intercontinental. Air Tahiti Nui counts New Zealand among the places its long-haul flights reach (atn-destinations), and the four countries are unchanged.

claims.note: Was 'Air Tahiti flies daily to most other islands in French Polynesia'. SEAC's 2025 table shows only 10 of the 46 public outer aerodromes with 730 or more commercial movements, the number a daily return flight needs (Bora Bora had 10,430, Raiatea 8,251); 36 had fewer. Air Moana is added: SEAC ranks it second to Air Tahiti by movements (about 5,300 flights in 2025) and credits its arrival with the growth on tourist routes; Tahiti Tourisme names both airlines; Wikipedia's infobox lists it among the airport's hub airlines. For the owner: this adds a second airline to a sentence that named one.

claims.claim: not enough level ground; built offshore rather than flatten sloping farmland
claims.wasBefore: There was not enough level ground on Tahiti, and rather than flatten large stretches of sloping farmland
claims.why: The reason rests on Wikipedia alone ('Because of limited level terrain, rather than leveling large stretches of sloping agricultural land'); no second source gives it. That the airport sits on reclaimed land just offshore is kept (see above).

claims.claim: laid on reclaimed land over the coral reef
claims.wasBefore: the airport was laid primarily on reclaimed land over the coral reef just offshore
claims.why: Reworded to 'mostly on reclaimed land just offshore': Wikipedia says on the coral reef and Tahiti Tourisme in the lagoon, so the text keeps only what both say.

claims.claim: takes an A380
claims.wasBefore: takes aircraft up to a 747 or A380
claims.why: The A380 rests on Wikipedia alone. The AIP's local rules for NTAA name code D and code E aircraft (the B747 among them) and no larger type. The 747 is kept (see above).

claims.claim: Canada by way of the States, and Chile
claims.wasBefore: Canada by way of the States, Chile
claims.why: Out of date or not a route from here, and on Wikipedia alone. SEAC's map of the 2025 scheduled international routes from Tahiti-Faa'a (Paris, Los Angeles, Seattle, San Francisco, Honolulu, Tokyo, Auckland, Nouméa, Nadi, Rarotonga) has no Santiago and no Canadian city, and Tahiti Tourisme's lists of departure cities, its Chilean edition included, name neither. 'Canada by way of the States' is a connection in the United States, not a flight from Tahiti.

claims.claim: Air Tahiti flies daily to most other islands
claims.wasBefore: Air Tahiti flies daily to most other islands in French Polynesia
claims.why: Not supported: SEAC's 2025 table shows fewer than 730 commercial movements a year (less than a daily return flight) at 36 of the 46 public outer aerodromes. Corrected to several times a day to the most popular islands, with Air Moana (see above).

claims.claim: Air Tahiti's head office on the airport
claims.wasBefore: Both Air Tahiti and Air Tahiti Nui have their head offices on the airport.
claims.why: Air Tahiti's head office rests on Wikipedia alone. Tahiti Tourisme gives only a Papeete PO box (BP 314); the AIP lists Air Tahiti's international handling office at Faa'a and its ATR heavy maintenance on the aerodrome, not its head office; airtahiti.com refused the earlier helper (403) and was not tried again. Air Tahiti Nui's head office is kept (see above).

claims.claim: buses from Papeete along the west coast freeway, which passes in front of the terminal
claims.wasBefore: Buses run in from Papeete along the west coast freeway, which passes directly in front of the terminal.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The AIP's transport list for the aerodrome (taxis, tour operators' buses, car rental) and Tahiti Tourisme's pages (its getting-around page says only that a bus service connects Papeete with the other districts) place no public bus at the airport, and nothing else puts the west coast road in front of the terminal. Softened to taxis and transfers (see above).

claims.claim: opened in 1960
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. No opening date on any page tried for the airport's history: SEAC's aerodromes page, its 2010 activity report and its 2021 highlights, and Tahiti Tourisme's history of Tahiti (saved as seac-aerodromes, seac-ra-2010, seac-faits-2021 and tt-history), nor SEAC's Manureva collection page, which lists 114 untitled magazine issues (not kept). That is more tries than the brief's two or three. The operator's own site (tahiti-aeroport.pf) answered 503 to the earlier helper and was not tried again.

claims.claim: more than 1.7 million passengers in 2025
claims.why: Held back: the old text has no passenger figure, so there is nothing for it to replace. SEAC counts 1,722,726 regular commercial passengers in 2025, up 2.9 per cent; UAF counts 1,804,602, up 8.3 per cent and 23 per cent above 2019 (the two define traffic differently). 'More than 1.7 million passengers in 2025' is true of both, if the owner wants it added.
